notes.statement: In 4 of 5 children of consanguineous Palestinian parents with a severe early-onset neuropathy, Yum et al. (2009) identified a homozygous c.628G>T transversion in the NEFL gene, resulting in a glu210-to-ter (E210X) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous and the unaffected sib did not carry the mutation; the mutation was not found in more than 11,000 individuals analyzed at a diagnostic laboratory.
quotes: At position 628 in the cDNA (c.628), a homozygous G>T transversion was detected (c.628G>T), predicted to result in a glutamate>AMBER change at position 210 (E210X), in all four affected children.
The E210X mutation has not been found in more than 11,000 individuals analyzed at Athena Diagnostics

notes.statement: Yum et al. (2009) reported that patients homozygous for NEFL E210X had motor nerve conduction velocities of 12 to 25 m/s, within the demyelinating range, with progressively reduced amplitudes with age, absent sensory responses, and prolonged visual evoked responses in 3 of 4, indicating subclinical CNS axonal involvement.
quotes: The median and ulnar motor responses were severely slowed, ranging from 12 to 25 m/s, and had progressively smaller amplitudes with age.
Visual evoked responses (VERs) were done in 2008, and were prolonged in three of four affected children (Table 1).

notes.statement: Yum et al. (2009) found that a sural nerve biopsy from a patient homozygous for NEFL E210X showed reduced numbers of myelinated axons, all less than 3 microns in diameter and lacking intermediate filaments. They concluded that the absence of large myelinated axons, rather than demyelination, likely explained the slowed conduction velocities.
quotes: Myelinated axons had microtubules, but intermediate filaments were not present (Fig. 4C and Supplemental Fig. 5).
the histological analysis of the biopsy indicates that the absence of large, myelinated axons is the likely explanation for the slowed conduction.

notes.statement: Yum et al. (2009) found that in SW-13 vim- cells, the E210X mutant did not form filaments, accumulated poorly, and did not disrupt filament assembly by wildtype NFL or the vimentin network, unlike the dominant Q333P mutant. They concluded that E210X causes a simple loss of function.
quotes: As shown in Fig. 5, the E210X mutant did not form filaments, but was typically found in a diffuse pattern, largely in the nucleus, with occasional cytoplasmic puncta in cells with higher levels of expression.
Thus, at least in these assays, the E210X mutant does not have a dominant effect.

notes.statement: Yum et al. (2009) proposed the term 'severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy' (SEOAN) for the disorder caused by homozygous NEFL E210X, and suggested that in OMIM nomenclature their patients should be designated CMT2B5.
quotes: we find the term “severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy” (SEOAN) is a more fitting name for their neuropathy
our patients should be called CMT2B5.

notes.statement: Abe et al. (2009) screened NEFL in 223 Japanese CMT patients who were negative for mutations in other known CMT genes and found heterozygous missense mutations in 5 unrelated patients and a homozygous nonsense mutation (Glu140Ter) in 1 patient.
quotes: We investigated NEFL in 223 Japanese CMT patients who were negative for PMP22, MPZ, GJB1, LITAF, EGR2, GDAP1, MTMR2 and PRX in the demyelinating form

notes.statement: Abe et al. (2009) concluded that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype, in contrast to missense mutations, which cause a dominant phenotype.
quotes: Results of our study show that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype, in contrast to missense mutations, which cause a dominant phenotype.

notes.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies for NEFL mutations. They found 6 disease-associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion, clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.
quotes: we screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies
We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.

notes.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) found that patients with NEFL mutations had early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype. Nerve conduction velocities were moderately to severely slowed.
quotes: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype. Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.

notes.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) concluded that the clinical variation in CMT depends on which gene is mutated and on the specific type of mutation. They suggested that NEFL mutations need to be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.
quotes: Our findings provide further evidence that the clinical variation observed in CMT depends on the gene mutated and the specific type of mutation, and we also suggest that NEFL mutations need to be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.
